brief: Three bases arranged around an empty spot, with a bay tray standing in that spot.

requirements.requirement: Three bases arranged around an empty spot
requirements.evidence: Three full base pieces — piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:2,0,0;full — grouped as one body (walls 0,1|1,0 and 1,0|2,0), each adjacent to the empty cell (1,1,0), which holds no base piece.

requirements.requirement: A bay tray standing in that empty spot
requirements.evidence: bay:0#1,1#bay1 — a full bay tray (hex-bin-bay-n-full-solid) — placed at the empty spot (1,1,0), bolted to all three surrounding bases, per the configurator's bay offer for that cell.

finish.summary: Removed the pre-existing base at (0,0), then built a trio of full bases at (1,0), (0,1) and (2,0) so they all touch the empty cell (1,1). Stood a full bay tray (plain solid) in that spot, where it bolts to all three bases. Open faces were capped and the wall joints bolted locked; check_build passes with meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three bases around an empty spot with a bay tray in the middle — I'll check the current build and where a bay tray can fit.

result.note: A bay stands in an empty cell with three bases around it. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
